title: Work & power
examples: If I push a box across the floor, how do I calculate the work done?
What is the difference between work and power?
Can you give me an example of calculating power in a real machine?

explain.say: Work done is the force you apply times the distance you move.
The formula for work is force times distance times the cosine of the angle.
Power is the rate at which work is done, or work divided by time.
The standard unit for work done is the joule, which is newton metres.
Power is measured in watts, which is joules per second.
For a real-life example, a car pulling a cart up a hill shows work and power.

faq.q: What is the difference between work and energy?
faq.a: Work and energy are related concepts in physics. Work is done when a force causes displacement. Energy is the capacity to do work.
asks: Are work and energy the same thing?
When I do work, do I use energy?

faq.q: Does the angle theta matter when calculating work?
faq.a: Yes, the angle matters because work only depends on the component of the force in the direction of motion. If the force is perpendicular to motion, the work done is zero.
asks: What happens if I pull something straight up?
When is cos theta equal to zero?

faq.q: How do I calculate power if I only know the force and distance?
faq.a: You cannot calculate power with just force and distance. You must also know the time taken to complete the work.
asks: Do I need time to find power?
Is power just about how fast something moves?

faq.q: What are the units for work and power?
faq.a: Work is measured in joules, and power is measured in watts. Remember that one watt is one joule per second.
asks: What is the unit for doing work?
How do I convert joules to watts?

faq.q: If the force is perpendicular to the movement, what is the work done?
faq.a: If the force is perpendicular to the direction of displacement, the work done is zero. Think of carrying a heavy box horizontally.
asks: Does lifting something count as work?
What is the work done by gravity on a horizontal object?

facts: Work done is calculated using the formula W equals F times d times cosine theta.
The unit for work done is the joule, symbol J, which is equivalent to newton metre.
Power is the rate of doing work, calculated as work divided by time.
The unit for power is the watt, symbol W, which is equal to joules per second.

quiz.say: A student pushes a box with a force of ten newtons over a distance of five metres at an angle of zero degrees. What is the work done?
quiz.why: Since the angle is zero degrees, the cosine is one, so work is simply force times distance: ten times five equals fifty joules.

wrong.0: This assumes the force is perpendicular to the movement, which is not the case here.
wrong.1: The answer must be in units of energy, not degrees.
wrong.3: This only uses the force and ignores the distance moved.

quiz.say: A machine does 200 joules of work in 10 seconds. What is the power output of the machine?
quiz.why: Power is work divided by time. Two hundred joules divided by ten seconds equals twenty watts.

wrong.1: This incorrectly multiplies the work by the time instead of dividing.
wrong.2: This only uses the time and ignores the work done.
wrong.3: The answer must be in units of power, not energy.

quiz.say: A person pulls a sled across flat ground with a force of 50 newtons at an angle of ninety degrees to the ground. What is the work done?
quiz.why: The cosine of ninety degrees is zero, so the work done by the pulling force is zero because it is perpendicular to the motion.

wrong.0: This incorrectly tries to divide the force by the angle.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes the angle is zero degrees.
wrong.3: While the units are correct for work, the calculation ignores the perpendicular angle.
